title: Government lifts ban on wheat exports, cites farmers’ interests amid depressed local prices
author: PTI
content_html:
The government on Monday (August 24, 2026) lifted the export ban on wheat and wheat products with immediate effect and said the decision is aimed at boosting farmers' income amid depressed domestic prices.

Early this year, the government had allowed the export of 50 lakh tonnes of wheat and 10 lakh tonnes of wheat products.

India, the world's second-largest wheat producer, had banned wheat exports in May 2022 as part of measures to control rising domestic prices.

"The export policy of wheat.... is revised from prohibited to free with immediate effect," according to notifications issued by the Directorate General of Foreign Trade.

The government has also removed the export ban on wheat flour and other products such as maida, semolina, and wholemeal atta, as per other notifications.

When asked about the decision, Food Secretary Sanjeev Chopra told PTI, "The export ban has been lifted in the interest of farmers. The domestic wheat prices are depressed currently. Allowing exports will increase the domestic market prices and encourage good sowing in the coming rabi season, and farmers will get better prices." On the impact of consumer prices, Mr. Chopra said there is adequate stock of wheat available in the country, sufficient to meet the demand and check prices.

The export of wheat, which was allowed earlier through issue of licence, has now been simplified, he added.

Out of 60 lakh tonnes allowed earlier, 2.5 lakh tonnes have been shipped so far, the secretary said.

India's wheat production stood at a record 120.65 million tonnes in the 2025-26 crop year (July-June) as against 117.94 million tonnes in the preceding year.

The Food Corporation of India (FCI), the government's nodal agency for the procurement and distribution of foodgrains, has nearly 49 million tonnes of wheat in buffer stock.

According to government data, the all-India average retail price of wheat stood at ₹31.46 per kg on Monday (August 24, 2026), while the rate of wheat flour at ₹37.3 per kg. The rates of wheat and wheat flour are flat compared to the year-ago period.

title: BJP leaders question Rahul Gandhi’s remarks on the Manusmriti and women’s rights
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leaders have questioned the remarks made by the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on the Manusmriti and women’s rights. BJP MP Nishikant Dubey quoted two verses from the text that emphasise respect for women, while Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma accused Mr. Gandhi of using women’s empowerment as a pretext to target Hinduism.

Mr. Sarma also asked how often the Congress leader had spoken against what he described as “patriarchal and medieval practices that persist under Sharia”.

During an interaction with female students in Maharashtra on August 22, 2026, Mr. Gandhi spoke against the “Manusmriti mindset”, called on students to “smash patriarchy”, and said women belonged to themselves, not to their fathers, husbands or sons.

On social media platform X, the Congress party shared a photograph of him with an attributed quote: “The Manusmriti states that a woman must never be independent. But I believe women should be independent. You may have relationships with your father, brother, husband, or son, but you do not belong to them. You belong to yourself.”

Responding to the post the same day, Mr. Dubey tagged a message to Mr. Gandhi’s X handle, saying: “Reading the Manusmriti may not be possible for you, @RahulGandhi ji. This is a shloka from the Manusmriti; read, understand, and speak. Because of the English language, do you know nothing about India’s Vedas, Puranas, scriptures, Ramayana, and Mahabharata?”

Mr. Dubey mentioned two verses from the Manusmriti, along with translations that read: “Where women are respected and worshipped, the gods reside; where they are not respected, all work and noble deeds bring no results.”

On Monday (August 24, 2026), Mr. Sarma posted on X: “Rahul Gandhi is no champion of women’s rights. He is simply a Hindu baiter, using the cause of women’s empowerment as a convenient smokescreen to target and discredit Hindu Dharma.”

“Consider this: how many times has he spoken with the same outrage against patriarchal and medieval practices that persist under Sharia? Never. While Sharia is foundational to Islamic jurisprudence, Manusmriti has no comparable scriptural authority in Hindu Dharma. It is not even a universally binding code for Hindus,” Mr. Sarma said.

“Yet ask yourself: how many times does Rahul Gandhi attack the Manusmriti, and how many times does he attack Sharia with the same fervour? The enduring strength of Hinduism lies in its unique ability to evolve, reform and adapt with time – as it has for millennia and as it will for eternity,” he said.

“Every Hindu must therefore ask: what is Rahul Gandhi’s real intent – championing women’s rights, or using them as a pretext to malign Hindu Dharma? Cong[ress] rhetoric on women’s rights rings hollow when measured against its own record. They betrayed our mothers and sisters by reversing the effect of the Shah Bano judgment,” Mr. Sarma added.

Stating that the Congress opposed the law against ‘Triple Talaq’, he alleged that just to “cling to power in Karnataka”, Mr. Gandhi had ensured “not a single woman found a place in the State Cabinet”.

“So here is a simple challenge to Rahul Gandhi: If women’s equality truly comes before politics, will he unequivocally support a Uniform Civil Code that guarantees equal rights irrespective of religion? Or will his idea of ‘women’s rights’ continue to begin and end with attacking Hinduism?” Mr. Sarma said.

title: Detect and deport illegal migrants, Amit Shah tells police chiefs
author: Vijaita Singh
content_html:
Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Monday (August 24, 2026) directed the security agencies to take strict measures against infiltration, asking the police chiefs to detect and deport illegal migrants. He was inaugurating the two-day National Security Strategies Conference-2026 (NSSC).

On Tuesday (August 25), the conference will discuss information warfare and its implications on national security and the need for a bio-security framework.

The Home Minister said an AI-based analysis of information available on Multi Agency Centres (MAC) platforms should be done to create standard operating procedures (SOPs) to counter various national security challenges.

The conference held in hybrid format was attended by over 850 participants from across the country. Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan, Director, Intelligence Bureau Mahesh Dixit and heads of Central Armed Police Force (CAPF) attended the conference in Delhi. Directors General of Police of States and Union Territories, young police officers working at the cutting-edge level and domain experts from specialised fields joined the conference through virtual mode, the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) said.

On the first day of the conference, discussions focused on critical aspects of national security, including response to counter-terrorism challenges, fusion, analysis and operationalisation of intelligence through MAC, vision document on narcotics control, detection and deportation of illegal migrants, a policy framework to combat cybercrime and proxy warfare by Pakistan.

For effective tackling of terrorism and radicalisation, Mr. Shah emphasised on training for implementation of the MHA’s PRAHAAR scheme, expediting trial by bringing back fugitives and using trial in absentia provisions and undertaking comprehensive and integrated approach while investigating Unlawful Activities Prevention Act (UAPA) cases.

The second day of the conference will focus on the threat landscape from sub-aerial systems and formulating countermeasures, securing the blue economy.

In pursuance to the directions of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, NSSC is being held every year in hybrid format since 2021, to find solutions to major national security challenges using the extensive experience of officers working at the grassroots level in collaboration with domain experts.

title: Will decide Tejpal plea against surrender before listing appeal against conviction: SC
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
A Single-Judge Bench of the Supreme Court on Monday (August 24, 2026) concluded that an appeal filed by journalist Tarun Tejpal against a 10-year sentence in a 2013 rape case cannot be listed for hearing without deciding his separate application seeking exemption from surrender.

“Until and unless, suitable orders are passed on the application seeking exemption from surrender, the appeal cannot be listed before the court. Therefore, the prayer made to list the matter before the court, without considering the application seeking exemption from surrender, cannot be accepted,” Justice Alok Aradhe recorded in a short order.

The court listed the case for August 25, and asked senior advocate Kapil Sibal, appearing for Tejpal, to address the Single Judge Bench on the merits of the application seeking exemption from surrender. Mr. Sibal had sought that the application be listed before the Court on August 31.

On the other hand, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the State of Goa, had opposed the plea while citing the Supreme Court Rules, 2013.

Mr. Mehta argued that the Rules were mandatory in nature that until and unless the appellant surrendered, his appeal should not be listed before the apex court.

The top law officer however submitted daily that the apex court had the power to even do away with the requirement of surrender.

On Monday, Tejpal’s plea was listed in chamber matters before a Single Judge Bench of Justice Aradhe. Chamber matters are heard to contest and settle procedural questions before the case is listed before a Regular Bench.

On August 20, Tejpal moved the court challenging the August 6 order of the Bombay High Court. Earlier, the Goa Government had appealed to the top court seeking an enhanced sentence for the former editor of Tehelka, contending that the case warranted imprisonment for life.

The Bombay High Court convicted Tejpal of rape and sentenced him to rigorous imprisonment for 10 years while overturning his acquittal by the trial court five years ago. Tejpal was convicted of raping a junior colleague inside a hotel elevator in 2013. The 62-year-old journalist had claimed he was a political victim.

title: Farmers’ body terms National Co-operative Development Corporation Act ‘anti-federal’
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
The National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC) Act, recently passed by Parliament, is an onslaught on the federal rights of States, the Samyukt Kisan Morcha said here in a statement. The umbrella organisation of farmer groups alleged that the NCDC Act would divert resources from the priority sector of agriculture and agriculture-based, rural industrial and infrastructure development, and that the new law was framed to suit the “corporate model of urban-centric development”.

Citing the Constitution’s Seventh Schedule, the SKM said “cooperation” was in the State list, and the NCDC Act of 2026 is a “naked intrusion” by the Union government into the powers of the States. “As per International Cooperative Alliance principles, autonomy and independence are basic principles of cooperation along with democratic control. The NCDC Act 2026 that permits NCDC to directly intervene in the cooperative societies and take their shares openly violates the basic principles of cooperation and facilitates centralisation of power into the hands of the Union government,” the SKM’s statement said.

The SKM argued that by directly extending financial assistance to cooperative societies, the NCDC would negate the control of State governments on its cooperatives, and centralise cooperative institutions under the power of the Union government for political dominance over States. “This reflects the authoritarian character of the corporate class fully endorsed by BJP-RSS (Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh) combine,” the statement added.

The Supreme Court, through an order given in 2021, had stated that the Union government has limited powers to intervene in cooperative societies, which are under State governments, the SKM said, and the new amendment had been brought to nullify the apex court’s order.

“Cooperatives are the soul of rural India and are capable of bringing widespread developments in the villages. The NCDC Act 2026 permits its operations to extend to non-agricultural sectors, abolish the stipulation of developing industries in the rural regions means the resources meant to use for agriculture and rural industrial and infrastructure expansion will be diverted for urban-centric development suitable for corporate development model,” the statement said.

title: Supreme Court asks Centre to respond to plea to reduce percentile for NEET-SS in-service candidates
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
The Supreme Court on Monday (August 24, 2026) asked the Centre to consider a plea by the Tamil Nadu Medical Officers Association seeking reduction of the cut-off or qualifying percentile for National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test-Super Speciality seats (NEET-SS) for in-service government doctors.

A Bench headed by Justice P.S. Narasimha heard senior advocate P. Wilson, for the association, on an application seeking the Centre to return 100% of the unfilled in-service seats to the State.

The Union Government had submitted that out of the 152 seats transferred by the State of Tamil Nadu, approximately 40 seats continued to remain vacant.

Mr. Wilson submitted that the entire 40 in-service seats must be returned to the State of Tamil Nadu, as 111 candidates were awaiting a reduction in the qualifying percentile.

Subsequently, the court turned to the Union Government to take a call on whether the qualifying percentile for Super Speciality admissions should be reduced. It posted the case for further hearing on August 31.

The association had challenged the “premature diversion” of 152 vacant Super Speciality seats earmarked for in-service government doctors in Tamil Nadu to the All India Quota. It had also sought protection of the State’s in-service reservation policy, pending a final decision on the reduction of the NEET-SS qualifying percentile.

The petition submitted that Tamil Nadu had earmarked 219 super speciality seats for in-service candidates for the academic year 2025-2026. Upon completion of two rounds of counselling, only 68 candidates had joined, leaving as many as 152 seats vacant.

“Over 111 in-service candidates remain on the waiting list and are legitimately anticipating reduction of the qualifying percentile in accordance with the consistent practice followed during previous academic sessions. A substantial number of these candidates narrowly missed the existing qualifying percentile and would become eligible if the qualifying percentile is reduced/relaxed,” the association said.

These candidates possessed a legitimate expectation that they would be considered for admission in the in-service category, it submitted.

title: Officials followed ‘standard practice’, sources say after Gor claims Indian side asked for ‘no questions’ in Modi-Trump event
author: Kallol Bhattacherjee
content_html:
Indian officials followed the "standard practice" of checking the modalities for public appearances by Prime Minister Narendra Modi ahead of his meeting with U.S. President Donald Trump on the sidelines of the G7 summit in France earlier this year, official sources said on Monday (August 24, 2026), hours after U.S. Ambassador Sergio Gor claimed that the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) had asked for the press event not to feature questions. Mr. Gor went on to say that Mr. Trump subsequently forgot about the purported request and went on to answer questions from journalists for 45 minutes.

“Discussions regarding arrangements for public appearances of leaders are normal practice ahead of any VVIP visit. In this regard, the Indian side communicated its standard practice for such visits,” a source said, referring to the interaction between Mr. Modi and Mr. Trump in Evian, France, on June 17, 2026.

Addressing a media conclave on Sunday (August 23), Mr. Gor had said that the MEA had an “ask” regarding making the meeting between the two leaders free of questions from the press. “We were behind the scenes, behind the stage, and at one point, it was just the President and I, and he asked me what the Indians were going to raise. We went over some topics,” said Mr. Gor.

According to Mr. Gor, Mr. Trump also wanted to know if the Indian delegation had any specific requests regarding the conduct of the event and he was told that the Indian side would prefer not to take questions.

“He said, ‘Do they have any asks?’ And the MEA had one ask,” Mr. Gor said. Mr. Trump, however, forgot about the Indian side’s “ask”, Mr. Gor claimed, and proceeded to answer questions. “A 45-minute press conference followed, and everything was on the table,” he said.

Official sources, however, pointed out that during the press interaction, all questions, both from U.S. and Indian presspersons, were aimed at Mr. Trump and that Mr. Modi was not asked any questions.

Congress reacts

Meanwhile, the Congress party said the office of the Prime Minister was being “diminished and disrespected”.

“This is not just about Narendra Modi. It is the office of India’s Prime Minister that is being diminished and disrespected,” Congress leader Pawan Khera said in a post on X. Mr. Khera said Mr. Gor’s remarks were revealing, suggesting that avoiding questions from the media was a regular practice under Mr. Modi. “Why is Modi so afraid of facing the media?” he asked.

In another post, Mr. Khera said Mr. Trump had not taken Mr. Modi’s concerns seriously. “A compromised PM is not taken seriously,” he said.

“It is painful to see what India has been reduced to under Narendra Modi. Once a formidable force. Today, taken for granted,” he added, while asking why Mr. Modi was “so afraid of press freedom — at home and abroad”.

Indian officials followed the "standard practice" of checking the modalities for public appearances by Prime Minister Narendra Modi ahead of his meeting with U.S. President Donald Trump on the sidelines of the G7 summit in France earlier this year, official sources said on Monday (August 24, 2026), hours after U.S. Ambassador Sergio Gor claimed that the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) had asked for the press event not to feature questions. Mr. Gor went on to say that Mr. Trump subsequently forgot about the purported request and went on to answer questions from journalists for 45 minutes.
“Discussions regarding arrangements for public appearances of leaders are normal practice ahead of any VVIP visit. In this regard, the Indian side communicated its standard practice for such visits,” a source said, referring to the interaction between Mr. Modi and Mr. Trump in Evian, France, on June 17, 2026.
Addressing a media conclave on Sunday (August 23), Mr. Gor had said that the MEA had an “ask” regarding making the meeting between the two leaders free of questions from the press. “We were behind the scenes, behind the stage, and at one point, it was just the President and I, and he asked me what the Indians were going to raise. We went over some topics,” said Mr. Gor.
According to Mr. Gor, Mr. Trump also wanted to know if the Indian delegation had any specific requests regarding the conduct of the event and he was told that the Indian side would prefer not to take questions.
“He said, ‘Do they have any asks?’ And the MEA had one ask,” Mr. Gor said. Mr. Trump, however, forgot about the Indian side’s “ask”, Mr. Gor claimed, and proceeded to answer questions. “A 45-minute press conference followed, and everything was on the table,” he said.
Official sources, however, pointed out that during the press interaction, all questions, both from U.S. and Indian presspersons, were aimed at Mr. Trump and that Mr. Modi was not asked any questions.
Congress reacts
Meanwhile, the Congress party said the office of the Prime Minister was being “diminished and disrespected”.
“This is not just about Narendra Modi. It is the office of India’s Prime Minister that is being diminished and disrespected,” Congress leader Pawan Khera said in a post on X. Mr. Khera said Mr. Gor’s remarks were revealing, suggesting that avoiding questions from the media was a regular practice under Mr. Modi. “Why is Modi so afraid of facing the media?” he asked.
In another post, Mr. Khera said Mr. Trump had not taken Mr. Modi’s concerns seriously. “A compromised PM is not taken seriously,” he said.
“It is painful to see what India has been reduced to under Narendra Modi. Once a formidable force. Today, taken for granted,” he added, while asking why Mr. Modi was “so afraid of press freedom — at home and abroad”.

title: Rules at tribal hostels undermining dignity of students: Rahul Gandhi
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Monday wrote to Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis alleging that rules governing tribal hostels were undermining the dignity and access to education of students and said Adivasi students had been on hunger strike for more than 10 days.

In his letter to Mr. Fadnavis, Mr. Gandhi followed up on interactions with students in Pune during the Chhatron ki Gunj (echoes of students) programme last Saturday. He said students from across Maharashtra had told him about hostel rules that “strip them of their dignity and shut off their path to education”.

Mr. Gandhi expressed particular concern over facilities for women, saying female students returning after an extended absence were required to undergo pregnancy tests and other medical examinations to establish their “fitness”.

“It is a humiliation that presumes them guilty until they prove otherwise,” he said, describing the requirement as an “attack on their dignity and their humanity”.

Mr. Gandhi flagged a rule barring those above 30 from hostel accommodation, saying it excluded many students still completing their studies or preparing for examinations.

He also alleged that hostels were unsafe and often lacked food, sanitation and medical care, with students suffering injuries and deaths, including from snake bites.

“These students are not asking for charity. They are demanding what is theirs by right,” Mr. Gandhi said, urging Mr. Fadnavis to hear the students’ concerns and resolve them immediately.

Earlier in the day, the party had sought a special committee to probe the deaths of tribal children allegedly due to malnutrition in Madhya Pradesh and of tribal girls following snakebite in Maharashtra and demanded action against officials found responsible.

Adivasi Congress chief Vikrant Bhuria also called for a safety audit of tribal hostels, citing alleged lapses in facilities in the two States.

Addressing a press conference here, Mr. Bhuria claimed that 22 children from the Baiga tribal community had died of malnutrition and related diseases in the Balaghat district of Madhya Pradesh.

He alleged that a nutritional meal delivered to households had been discontinued for six months and that the nearest primary health centre was 20 km away. Vaccination coverage in the area was also below 80%, he claimed.

Also read: Faith healing poses challenge to authorities as outbreak kills seven tribal children in Madhya Pradesh

“I had asked in the Madhya Pradesh Legislative Assembly how much budget was allocated for preventing malnutrition in the State’s tribal blocks and projects from 2020 to 2025, and how much of it was spent. The response was extremely concerning. The government said malnourished children are given a nutritional meal worth only ₹12 per day,” he said.

Turning to Maharashtra, he alleged that more than 70 girls at a tribal hostel in Gadchiroli were made to sleep on the floor in a single room. Six girls were hospitalised following a snakebite incident, of whom three died, he claimed.

Mr. Bhuria said students protesting in Nashik were continuing their hunger strike, demanding better facilities at tribal hostels. He sought a probe into the Balaghat deaths and action against officials found responsible.

title: Uproar after Allahabad High Court refer Divisional Commissioner's conduct for criminal contempt
author: Mayank Kumar
content_html:
Uproar took place on Monday (August 24, 2026) after Devipatan Divisional Commissioner Durga Shakti Nagpal allegedly attempted to influence a Civil Judge (Senior Division), Shabina Khan, in Gonda.

She is handling a civil suit, with social activists demanding a high-level investigation by the State government, and the Allahabad High Court referred the conduct to the court dealing with criminal contempt matters on August 21. 

In the matter, the Civil Judge, Gonda, in a letter to the District Judge, said she received repeated calls while on leave on July 15, 2026 from a number linked to the Commissioner’s office.

Later, she said she got a call from Commissioner Durga Shakti Nagpal, who wanted to discuss the pending suit and asked pointed questions about how long she intended to stay on leave. The judge said the calls and the tone used amounted to interference. 

In the matter, Allahabad High Court Justice Syed Qamar Hasan Rizvi on Friday (August 21, 2026) held that the allegations of pressure on the judicial officer could not simply be ignored and directed that the matter be placed before the appropriate bench dealing with criminal contempt.

Justice Rizvi noted that the District Judge, Gonda, had already transferred the suit to another equivalent court on 9 August 2026, so the transfer plea had lost its purpose. But held that the tone of the alleged conversation showed the judge was being pressured, and that courts cannot look away at insulting language used against a Presiding Officer. The Court directed that the matter be placed before the appropriate contempt bench after seeking directions from the Chief Justice or the Senior Judge.

Lucknow-based social activist Amitabh Thakur called for an independent, high-level inquiry into the matter and demanded that the Chief Secretary of U.P. immediately transfer Durga Shakti Nagpal from the Devipatan (Gonda) Division.

“I have sent a letter to the Chief Secretary of Uttar Pradesh demanding the transfer of Gonda (Devipatan) Commissioner Durga Shakti Nagpal and an independent high-level inquiry into the entire matter in light of an order passed by the Lucknow Bench of the Allahabad High Court on Friday (August 21, 2026), Mr. Thakur told The Hindu. 

“The telephonic conversation between Gonda’s Civil Judge (Senior Division) and the Divisional Commissioner was, prima facie an attempt to influence a judicial officer, in accordance with the order of the High Court. I demanded that the Chief Secretary immediately transfer Durga Shakti Nagpal from Gonda Division and constitute an independent high-level administrative inquiry into the telephonic conversation with the judicial officer and the events that followed,” he added.

Mr. Thakur has also demanded that clear protocols and necessary administrative instructions be issued regarding executive officials contacting judicial officers in connection with pending judicial cases.

The Divisional Commissioner gave a different account of the events and said in a letter to the Administrative Judge, Gonda that she called only to check on the judge’s leave status since the case, pending nearly 30 years and involving land needed for her office building, required expediting, and that the judge reacted with anger and later declared in open court that she would not hear the matter further.
